headline: DA Finance Chief Steps Back Amid R4bn Probe
script: Big political story: the DA has just pulled its own finance chief, Mark Burke, off Parliament's finance committees. Why? His fintech company Kastelo is under Reserve Bank investigation over roughly R4 billion in alleged exchange-control violations. Here's the wild part: court findings show clients earning about R15,000 a month were allegedly given loans of R249,000, just so the company could tap their personal offshore allowances. A Joburg court already dismissed Kastelo's bid to unfreeze its accounts and hit them with punitive costs. The DA initially defended Burke, then did a 24-hour about-turn after pressure from the ANC and EFF. Why should you care? This is the same committee meant to watch over YOUR money and the institutions protecting it. When the watchdog's own house needs watching, that's a real accountability test, months before you vote.
why_it_matters: It shows how financial regulation and political accountability directly affect trust in the institutions protecting young South Africans' money and savings.
